utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam, and good afternoon to you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good afternoon to you too. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. Also good afternoon to the Defence. I'm here with co-counsel, Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good afternoon to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Vasvija Vidovic. Together with Mr. John Jones, I represent Mr. Naser Oric before this Tribunal. We have with us our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts. Good afternoon to my colleagues from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic. And good afternoon to you and your team. Let's deal with some preliminaries. Preliminary number one, the sitting scheduled for Thursday, May 12th, which was scheduled for the afternoon will now be in the morning. So please make note of it. All right. The other thing is this: You were supposed to tell me yesterday, come back -- report, Mr. Wubben, on the suggestion that we made the day before as to whether you would entertain the idea of having those two or three witnesses on the chain of custody testify by means of a written statement rather than orally here -- or rather than viva voce. And you were supposed to come back to me yesterday. I forgot to ask you and probably you forgot to tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. Indeed, Your Honours, I should have triggered it myself. But in the line of that, I can update you further of the outcome. A couple of days ago --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- indeed I invited Defence counsel to learn from their position in that respect. They requested me two days to -- to study and to learn from the facts to give their position. And today I update myself of the final outcome of it. The Defence requested me, at least today, to study further and to get back to me by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. That's fair enough. We will wait. We will wait. The idea, of course -- I want to make myself clear, that if this procedure is adopted, then there will of course -- the cross-examination will be reserved for the Defence. In other words, they still have to come, but they will come for cross-examination and they don't need to come for the examination-in-chief --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Unless -- unless it is not 89(F), Your Honour, but 92 bis, and that was my first aim --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And I understand and I --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please accept that we have an open discussion in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Yes, Madam Vidovic, do you want to contribute any remarks on this?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we need another day to consider this motion and to see whether we can agree on these witnesses not needing to appear. But I want to say one thing, Your Honours, cooperation must be mutual. I have asked Mr. Wubben to confirm that if we agree that we do not need to cross-examine these witnesses, we have no resources left to replace these witnesses with other witnesses. I asked for this confirmation, but Mr. Wubben was not ready to provide a reply. That is why we are still considering this and we need more time to keep considering. If this happens, we believe it would be entirely unfounded and unreasonable. And our position would be -- would become very difficult. Ever since we found out about the names of these people, our investigators have been busy investigating. This would imply that your investigators would need to under take further investigations for which we have neither time nor resources. This is one confirmation I would like to have from Mr. Wubben. As soon as this confirmation is provided, I believe we will be able to give you our decision very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We will await further, and when you are in a position to report in a definitive manner, please let us know, tell us. All right? Any further preliminaries. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, to inform Your Honours, the coming witness, C003, will not need protective measures. And in addition to yesterday's request for further information, the Prosecution needs definitely also tomorrow for the proofing of that witness. So we are happy to start on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I understand that, and I think there is nothing that we can do. Yes, anything from your side, Madam Vidovic, any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's bring the witness in. The witness -- MR. DI FAZIO: Could we -- could I just before that happens. Just one very brief matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: As a matter of courtesy, I think, to inform you about something regarding the next witness. I had the opportunity of speaking with Defence counsel before you came in and raised the issue of whether or not I need evidence from this witness regarding the methodology of the taking of the cassettes that you've heard about in previous evidence in this case and the transcripts and the creation of transcripts from those cassettes and the operation of the machine with the lights and so on, of which there has already been evidence in this case. I took the view that if that evidence was not seriously contested by the Defence or a matter of concern to them, then I could expedite things today by not leading evidence again on that topic. And they very helpfully informed me that is so, that that material is not in contention. So I don't intend to lead that sort of evidence today, unless of course you, meaning the Trial Chamber, has a particular need for me to do it again. In other words, the Prosecution will reply on the testimony from the previous -- previous witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And coming from the jurisdiction you come from, you know exactly what to expect from us. This is your case, not ours, Mr. -- MR. DI FAZIO: Certainly, certainly. I am clear about what I want to do and I intend to do that, but only -- unless the Trial Chamber has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Listen, the position very simply put is that if Defence has no problems to -- in living with that, why should we? MR. DI FAZIO: With respect, if Your Honours please, I think all -- both the Defence and the Prosecution have made it clear that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. MR. DI FAZIO: It's not a matter of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If, however, at any point in time -- I mean, please don't consider yourself bound by this mutual agreement that as the testimony -- MR. DI FAZIO: Develops --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- develops, there might be the need to put some questions and then you are free to put the questions, et cetera. The only reservation I make is the following: That if you finish your examination-in-chief without raising this matter and there is no justification for the issue to be raised by the Defence and they do raise it nonetheless, then of course you will have a right to visit -- but it's the normal procedure that you are familiar with in any case. So let's -- okay. Do you anticipate we could finish today? MR. DI FAZIO: I am anticipating that if I follow this course of action --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In less than an hour. MR. DI FAZIO: I could be finished by the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. MR. DI FAZIO: I would only ask that the Defence merely put on the record that what I've said accurately reflects their position.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, I was going to do that. Firstly it's not in contention the system involving tapes and the rest of it. So as I did indicate to my learned friend, there is no problem either leading on that or passing over the subject all together. And as for the rest of the testimony, most of it is not in contention, so again I indicated to my learned friend that he can lead pretty much as much as he needs to. It may purely be that in cross-examination I'll confirm that the witness doesn't know about certain things, but I wouldn't go into it beyond that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed. I want to make sure -- one moment, usher, please. I want to make sure that the technicians and the rest know about the protective measures. We have a pseudonym, we have visual or facial and voice distortion in place, but we will be proceeding in open session except insofar as some questions may be put which, if answered, could reveal the witness's identity. For those, we could go into private session. MR. DI FAZIO: I've got about three that will require that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. All right. So I suppose -- let's bring the witness in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness's microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness's microphone is off. Yes. Good afternoon to you and welcome to this Tribunal. You are soon going to be -- to start giving evidence in this case, which the Prosecutor has -- Prosecution has instituted against Naser Oric. Before you start giving evidence, our rules require that you make a solemn declaration equivalent to an oath, in a sense that you undertake at -- throughout your testimony you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text on this solemn undertaking -- solemn declaration is contained on a piece of paper that is being passed on to you by Madam Usher. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please make yourself comfortable and take a seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me explain to you a little bit -- a few matters before you start giving evidence. You asked for and we decided to grant you certain protective measures. These protective measures we granted you because we felt that in the circumstances they are necessary, they are justified. And the -- the purpose of -- or the raison d'etre of these protective measures is to hide your identity from the public. As a result, you will not be referred to by your name but by a number. And you will be referred to in the records of this Tribunal and of this case as a Witness C009. Also, anyone who will be following these proceedings from outside this courtroom will not be able to see your face, or any part of your body for that matter, and also will not be able to hear your voice. Your face will appear as you are going to see on your monitor now. If you look at your monitor, please focus the camera or -- yes. That's how others will see you. And I can't -- I can't tell you how others will hear your voice, but your voice will be distorted. Otherwise, the proceedings will be held in open session; in other words, being outside of this courtroom will be able to know what questions you are being asked and what answers you are giving, but you will -- they will not be able to know who it is. For the first few questions, which will deal with who you are and therefore which could reveal your identity, we are not going to stay in open session, we will go into closed session or private session, so that whatever is said will remain inside these four walls. All right? Is that to your satisfaction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So I leave you in the hands of Mr. Di Fazio, who will be leading you in cross -- examining you in-chief. He will then be followed by Mr. Jones, who is co-counsel for Naser Oric. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, are we going into private session? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, my apologies. I thought we were already there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, we are not in private session. Let's go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document which has been shown to the witness and confirmed by her is given Exhibit Number P?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 535, and this will be entered and kept under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, it's not in dispute that your duties involved the transcription of intercepted telephone calls during the period 1992 and 1993, and it's also not in dispute that you came to The Hague recently and that you were shown a number of documents. And I want to simply expedite matters now and take you through some of the documents that you were shown in the course of proofing in the last few days. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P348. And this document is also in Sanction, as are all of the exhibits I will refer to this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's easier. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you have a photocopy of a document. The first question: Is that your handwriting? Flick through the document and tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes, this is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. There are some notations or endorsements on the document that I want to take you to. At the commencement of the document you will see an endorsement saying "Telephone Z2." Can you explain to Their Honours what "Telephone Z2" is, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Z2 is the second reel-to-reel recorder which was used to tape conversations. There was a total of 12. Z2 is the second. This is the code for that particular reel-to-reel recorder used for taping conversations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It does not refer to a particular telephone that was being targeted for intercept purposes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: It does refer to a specific telephone, but we didn't know the number of that telephone, only the technicians did. And all we would receive was a code as a reference to a certain telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not in dispute that what follows throughout the document is a transcript of recordings made by tape. Those recordings, were they recordings of conversations held on a telephone known to you as telephone Z2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes, those are the conversations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, where was telephone Z2 located, if you know? And if you don't know, that's fine; but if you do know, tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: I'm not sure right now. There were three phones. There was a group of three telephones sharing the same code. I'm not sure which one was which, or rather I can't remember right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This group of telephones, were they located, to your knowledge and always to your knowledge, were they located in a particular place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This group of telephones, do you know where they were physically located, the ones that were being listened to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: As far as I remember, one was at the supreme staff; another was a home telephone line; and there was a third one which I think belonged to an office but I can't remember the name of the office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. There's an endorsement in this document saying: "Telephone used by Skup." Can you explain to the Trial Chamber the meaning of "Skup." What or who is Skup?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Skup was a code, a code name for Sefer Halilovic's telephones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next endorsements that appear are these: It says: "Conversation held on the 28th of October, 1992." And underneath that: "Reported on the 28th of October, 1992." Can you explain to Their Honours the significance of those two endorsements. What does it mean the conversation was held on that date and what does it mean it was reported on that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: The conversation took place on the 28th of October, the same day a report is submitted to the bosses, that's on the 28th of October. So that's what these two references mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the report that is mentioned there what follows in that document, namely your handwritten notes? Are in fact your handwritten notes the report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes. This is my handwriting and I produced this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that. That's fine. But if you look at the document -- it's only a small matter and don't worry too much. But if you look at the document it says the conversation happened on that date and it was reported on that date. Now, the report, the report itself, when you talk -- when this says -- refers to a report or it being reported, is that in fact the handwritten notes that you've just spoken about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: These are not my notes. This is the exact conversation that was taped, word to word.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Your transcript, shall we say then, is that the report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And that's an important clarification. I appreciate it. Thank you. Just continue through the document. It says -- there's a reference there to: "001 counter number," and that appears throughout the document with different numbers, but that endorsement counter number continues to appear. Just briefly explain to the Trial Chamber what the meaning of counter number is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: 001 revolutions. Is that what you mean? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Just tell the Trial Chamber what it means, what it's a reference to, if it's got anything to do with cassette tapes and putting them in the machine and running them and seeing at what point of the cassette. You know it best, so you tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: It's like this: The tape is placed in a tape recorder. There's a counter that is set to 0. As soon as the conversation begins, the counter starts to revolve. This is a way of marking conversation on a given tape. We count the number of revolutions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you look at the first what appears to be portion of conversation in this document, you will see that there's a -- a code for the speakers, the people who were speaking the words that are contained in the transcript. So it starts off with the endorsement Najetovic called a Skup location, and asked a woman who answered the phone to leave the following message to Sakib or the commander and then follows with what appears to be conversation with N and X. Who is N?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: N is the person indicated at the beginning, Najetovic, and he was the one who is called the object referred to as Skup.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. There's also a person X, who is X?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: X is a secretary who worked at the staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you -- when you created these notice, or rather this transcript I should say, did you know the precise identity of the person X?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: No. And that's why she was marked as person X.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, and that's what I was driving at. The use of X in this transcript and in other transcripts, did that -- was that a method that you used to identify that someone was speaking but you didn't know who they were, their precise identity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you use that basic system, using the X to designate a speaker but an unknown identity throughout transcripts when you were making notice of conversations in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes. Unless person X accidentally happened to introduce themselves during the conversation of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you then change the designation from X to another initial now that you knew the real identity of the speaker?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: At that point, X would become the initial of the identified person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let -- look at the next section in the document. It's prefaced with the words "Asim from Visoko calling the commander." And then the conversation is set out and you've got apparently two speakers there, someone designated with A and someone designated with a letter K. Who is A?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: A in this case stands for Asim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And K?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: K stands for commander. That's how Sefer was referred to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the word "komandant" in B -- in your language, is it spelled with the letter K -- does it start with the letter K, the word "komandant," meaning commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you look at the last portion of conversation in that document following 134 counter number, you see another conversation apparently with someone called Rasim. And again, is K the initial for the commander and R the initial for Rasim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Did you use K to designate Sefer Halilovic in transcripts that you created throughout 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Depending on how he was addressed. If he was addressed by his name, then we would write down the first letter of his name; if not, if he was addressed as commander, we would do it this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how would you know that the person speaking, when he was only addressed as commander, was in fact Sefer Halilovic? How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: At the beginning, you have to get used to a voice. And later, once you've heard the same voice several times, you do start recognising it. You do start recognising voices once you're familiar with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. And was that part of your duties, to become acquainted with the voices of people who were being targeted, so to speak, by these -- by these intercepts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes. It did take some time for us to get used to the voices there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sure it did, but what I'm asking is this: Were you tasked with that? Was a part of your job to find out -- to become familiar with the voices so you could carry out your duties? Did your bosses want you to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P349.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Firstly, I want you to just look at the -- the -- the notations at the beginning of this document, and you will see that there's talk of a department and a date, a telephone, reference to something called Skup, conversation date, and so on. Is all the evidence that you've given -- just given in court this afternoon also apply to these notations? In other words, did they have the same meaning? Is Skup here Sefer Halilovic? Was the conversation in fact heard on the 28th of October, 1992? Was it in fact transcribed by you on the same day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes to all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And look at the body of the document and can you please tell us if that is your handwriting? In fact, look at the entire document, just skim through it, and tell us, is that your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes. Throughout the document the handwriting is mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I think we can finish up quickly with this document. I just take you through the various conversations. Again, first portion of the document deals with an apparent conversation between someone called K and someone called R. Again, is that the commander -- sorry, does K stand for commander, namely Sefer Halilovic, and is R the person called Rasim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And if you continue flicking through the document you come to one last portion of conversation between apparent -- between different speakers, and it commences at counter number 242. MR. DI FAZIO: Page 8, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you find that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It's apparently a conversation between Dzemo Merdan calling the commander and then follows the K and the DZ. Is the K Sefer Halilovic and is the DZ a reference to the person Dzemo Merdan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before the witness is shown the next document. After the name of Dzemo Merdan, there is in brackets Zenica. Is that his nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. This is Zenica in brackets. Zenica is the town from which he called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honour. Can the witness be shown the next exhibit, which is -- sorry -- I'm sorry, it wasn't P349. It's P350. Your Honours, could I just inquire of you before I proceed with this document. Do you have the English exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 350? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I think if you look -- my document -- my English equivalent translation finishes at the -- at the bottom it says page 7 of 7; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I've been through it and I don't think that the B/C/S goes as far as that and I think that the English -- that page is extraneous, it's extra, so to speak. I think if you look at the B/C/S, the B/C/S version will finish at 229 and it says Krai, K-r-a-i. And if you look at page 6 of 7, do you see that in the English, page 6 of 7?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Uh-huh. MR. DI FAZIO: That's where 229 ends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS

utterances.text: All right. And again if you could just confirm what may be obvious to many. The conversants are designated by letters S, is that Sefer Halilovic, and is A Andjelko Makar?

utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.text: And while we're on this document, I'd like to take you to one other common feature that I haven't fully asked you to explain. utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what you've just described, this formula that -- or method that was adopted, was that consistent throughout 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: No paper could be forwarded without a protocol number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I've finished with that document. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown P353.

utterances.text: Very simple questions again. I can put the one question and save time. Can you look at this document, tell us if your handwriting appears, and tell us if the Z is a reference to Zeljko Knez and the S is a reference to Sefer Halilovic speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown 357. All right.

utterances.text: Again, tell us if this is your handwriting throughout this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- I just want to look at the identity of the conversants, people speaking, in a little more detail. utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the conversation develops, a third person seems to come into the conversation. utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's quickly move through this one. Go to the section of the transcript that deals with counter number 93, preceded by 3 -- the number -- triple X. Again, in that part of the conversation is S a reference to Sefer Halilovic and R a reference to Ramiz Suvalic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: I don't know. We recorded in the transcript only the words that they used when they introduced themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you? MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P359.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you skipping 358? MR. DI FAZIO: My case manager just pointed it out to me. Would Your Honours just give me a moment to look at that. Yes, I am. Well -- yes, I am, yes. 359. utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Have a look at this exhibit and please tell us if it -- it's your handwriting and whether you created it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes, this is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On the exhibits that we've seen so far, the transcripts that you provided have an endorsement for telephone that has telephone Z2. This one has written on it telephone Z4. utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: I said at the beginning that three of Sefer's lines were intercepted and this is one of them. One of them was in the staff, one was his telephone at home, and the third one was in some office but I can't remember where that office was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it the case that telephone Z4 was one of those three that you've just talked about, either the one at the staff or at his home or in some office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you have any idea where this office might be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: I don't even know where the staff was, the supreme staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. No problem. But can you tell us this: Do you know if the Z4 telephone was in an office at the staff or if you don't know that at all, you can't say for sure, please make it clear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: I'm not sure after such a long time. I don't know where each of these telephones were physically. I can't be sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, let's go through the conversation. It will take us a little while, but I think we can deal with it reasonably quickly. utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you wary about using the designation K, since you used it so often or since you used it on several occasions with respect -- for Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes. We were already very familiar with the voices. So we could designate him by letter K. Generally everybody referred to him as commander, those who knew him well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. I understand that. Thank you for explaining that. In this particular case -- in this particular case, the commander, Sefer Halilovic, is in fact speaking. Any reason why you didn't use the letter K for him? And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry. Would Your Honours just give me a moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Continue on to the next part of the conversation, counter number 084. You see your endorsement there, Sefer H. Is that Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.text: And someone called Ibrahim. Do you know the full name of the person Ibrahim or you've got no idea?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: If he had introduced himself by his full name, I'm sure that this would have been recorded. But obviously he didn't, and that's why we recorded only his first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then appears next to it at this endorsement in brackets, "Srebrenica - radio-communication." What's that mean? What does that mean?

utterances.text: This means that the conversation took place using Sefer's telephone. Probably the only way was from Srebrenica by radio link, but this phone here is Sefer's phone in the office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But that's your handwriting, the words "Srebrenica - radio-communication," is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the tape you were listening to was, as far as you were aware, a conversation recorded on one of Sefer Halilovic's telephones or telephones that he had access to. Correct?

utterances.text: Probably this radio communication had been announced or you could tell by the sound of it that a radio was being used, but that's all I can remember. utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- thinking back to the period 1992/1993, were you able to recognise when a conversation over one of the target telephones was employing -- was being facilitated by radio communications? utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: We weren't trained to recognise that kind of thing. You either hear the switch being made or there is an announcement of radio communication usually at the beginning of any conversation that takes place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you comment on the -- your level of certainty or satisfaction that radio communications were being used -- let me rephrase that question perhaps. utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: I had to be positive, absolutely positive that radio communications were being used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I've understood your evidence correctly, your certainty, your degree of satisfaction came from two sources, either what the speakers themselves said or clicks and other noises that you heard when listening to the tape of the conversation. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. And the conversation that follows, S, is that a reference to Sefer Halilovic, and I, is that a reference to the man Ibrahim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Continue on to the next counter number from 440 onwards, and again there's a conversation between apparently Arif Pasalic and Sefer Halilovic. Is A Arif and is S Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: All right. Continue now to the next counter number 080, and that's a conversation between someone called Naser and Sefer Halilovic apparently. Does the N refer to the person called Naser and does the S refer to the person Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber who Naser is?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Continue to the 185 counter number. And -- again it's self-explanatory. Someone called Sliskovic from the Ministry of Defence calling Sefer H. Is Sl Sliskovic and is the simple S Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness now be shown P361.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, look at the document and tell us if that's your handwriting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From counter 057, Hazim Sadic is apparently speaking to Sefer Halilovic. And, again, is S Sefer Halilovic and is the H Hazim Sadic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009

utterances.text: Continue until you get to counter number 260. And again the conversation -- does the S represent Sefer Halilovic and is the N Mr. Oric, Naser Oric?

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes. This is a conversation launched from the Z4 phone, the one referred to as Skup.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, this would be an appropriate time. I've got one more exhibit and two or three more questions and I'll be finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Unless you prefer, I mean, subject to Mr. Jones agreeing to this of course, to go on for the next few minutes that you require, finish your examination-in-chief, then we'll have a break, and we'll start with the examination afterwards. MR. DI FAZIO: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: After you -- it's up to you, provided we are not talking of more than ten minutes. MR. DI FAZIO: I wouldn't have thought so, no. I think I can finish in ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Can I have the okay from -- yes. And the technical staff. I can't see behind Mr. Di Fazio. Yeah, okay. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P363.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you identify this as document as being created by your hand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.text: All right. I might finish even sooner than I thought. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours -- sorry.

utterances.text: Witness -- MR. DI FAZIO: I've finished with that exhibit. Thanks. And could the witness be shown Exhibit P359. And can the witness be shown Exhibit P359 again.

utterances.text: And, Witness, turn please to counter 080. It's apparently a conversation between Naser and Sefer Halilovic. Do you have that? MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours will find it at page 6 of 9 it says.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] 084 -- what I have is Sefer and Ibrahim. There's something wrong, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's behind -- usher, it's behind counter number 080. MR. DI FAZIO: I think I'll probably find it on the B/C/S and be able to take them straight to the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's on page 13 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 13. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you have it? utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: It very much depended on how he introduced himself. If he introduced himself by his first and last name, that's what I would write down; if he only would use his first name, I would only write down his first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any memory of recording conversations between Sefer Halilovic and any other person called Naser in the years 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C009
utterances.text: No. For the most part, those were contacts between Sefer Halilovic and Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I have no further questions.

utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. We'll have a break now. Mr. Jones, you are in a position now to more or less give us a clue as to how long you will be cross-examining the witness.

utterances.text: So let's have a 30-minute break. Thank you.
